result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_gnm_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add an Erdős-Rényi G(n,m) random graph to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3845-L3909){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_gnm_graph( n, m, directed=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![G(n, m) random graph](/assets/graphs/add-gnm-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three random graphs on the same ring of eight nodes with exactly m=4, 8, and 12 edges. The edge count is fixed by m while which pairs get joined is random." width="100%"} Creates a graph with `n` nodes and exactly m randomly placed edges. This model is useful for generating random graphs with a fixed number of edges. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes to add. [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of edges to create. [directed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[bool]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : If provided and differs from graph's directed setting, creates temporary graph with specified directedness. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for reproducibility. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Unlike `add_gnp_graph()`, which samples edges probabilistically, this fixes the exact number of edges -- `m=100` always produces exactly `100` edges, regardless of seed: ::: {#259af6ca .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_gnm_graph(n=50, m=100, seed=23) ) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (50, 100) ``` ::: :::
